claim: Custom slash commands have been merged into skills: .claude/commands/x.md and .claude/skills/x/SKILL.md both create /x, and old command files keep working.

evidence.quote: Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way.
Command files : a Markdown file in .claude/commands/ is the older format and still works. It supports the same frontmatter except name and paths .
Merged slash commands and skills, simplifying the mental model with no change in behavior

claim: In a skill, $ARGUMENTS is everything typed after the name; $ARGUMENTS[N] or $N gives one argument counting from 0; an 'arguments' frontmatter list gives named placeholders such as $issue.

evidence.quote: When no placeholder receives an argument, Claude Code appends them as ARGUMENTS: <value> .
Access a specific argument by 0-based index, such as $ARGUMENTS[0] for the first argument.
Named positional arguments for $name substitution in the skill content. Accepts a space-separated string or a YAML list. Names map to argument positions in order.

claim: Through claude -p (or the Agent SDK), a prompt of the form '/skill arg1 arg2' loads only the first skill and treats the rest of the line as its arguments.

evidence.quote: Through the Agent SDK or claude -p , Claude Code loads only the first skill, with the rest of the line as its arguments.
User-invoked skills and custom commands work. Include /skill-name in the prompt string and Claude Code expands it before running.

claim: --bare is the documented recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls; it skips hooks, skills, commands, MCP servers, CLAUDE.md and memory, and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or an apiKeyHelper) because it does not use a subscription login.

evidence.quote: --bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release.

claim: With Claude Code v2.1.302 or later, a claude -p run with no permission mode set starts in Manual mode, where a call that needs approval is denied (rather than waiting) unless something approves it, such as an --allowedTools rule, a PermissionRequest hook or --permission-prompt-tool.

evidence.quote: In a Manual mode claude -p run, a call that needs approval is denied unless something approves it, such as a PermissionRequest hook or a --permission-prompt-tool .
